payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the mug positioned to the right of the headphones; fail if it clearly shows the mug is not to their right; unknown if their relative position cannot be determined. For R1, complete if this check passes; absent if it fails and no requested change has progressed; partial if the mug has moved toward the requested position but is not yet to the right; unknown if required evidence remains unresolved. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Compare the mug’s visible position with the headphones in the image. Judge the requested spatial relationship, without requiring a particular editing technique.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the visible mug is positioned to the right of the headphones.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image clearly shows a mug and headphones, and their relative positions are observable: the mug is to the right of the headphones. Both objects are identifiable enough for comparison.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too broad and its traces appear to judge the requested relation from the edited image alone. In the source, there is one blue mug left of the headphones; in the edited image, the headphones are altered and there are two visible mugs, one on each side. The right-hand mug may satisfy the final positional relation, but that alone does not establish that the original mug was moved there or that the requested edit is complete; the left-hand mug and blurred blue region also make object identity and edit continuity ambiguous. Tighten the binding to the original mug and headphones, and make the criterion assess progress from source to edited image as well as the final relation: distinguish a completed move from partial progress such as duplication or an unresolved identity match. Do not force “partial” from the reference label; require image-grounded evidence for the classification, and use unknown if identity or change cannot be resolved. The two support observations are highly confident but not independent (s2 depends on s1), so avoid treating their agreement as corroboration. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; this is a semantic evidence/binding and criterion issue.

response.content: {"text":"The binding and criterion should compare the source and edited images, not merely ask whether any visible mug is right of the headphones. Bind the target to the original blue mug using observable appearance and location, then assess whether that same object’s requested relocation is evidenced; explicitly distinguish a final right-side relation from duplication or an unresolved identity match. Here the edited image shows two mugs, headphones that differ from the source, and a blurred blue region where the original mug was, so the right-hand mug alone does not establish completion, while the left mug/blur may indicate progress but leave continuity uncertain. Require evidence for both identity/change and final relation, and preserve unknown when those cannot be resolved rather than inferring a label from the reference. Treat the dependent, high-confidence support traces as one observation, not corroboration. This is a semantic binding/evidence issue; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported."}
